newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities leads UK utilities higher.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities leads UK utilities higher.

text.p: United Utilities led UK electricity and water shares higher in a weaker market on Friday as safe-haven buying and recent broker recommendations boosted the sectors, dealers said.

By 1612 GMT United Utilities was 12-1/2p stronger at 640, after reaching a record high of 645. Severn Trent was a penny higher at 683-1/2, Yorkshire Water firmed 5-1/2p to 713-1/2 and Hyder firmed 11p to 753-1/2.
Electricity firms also performed well. Powergen was up seven pence at 594, National Power gained 11p to 478-1/2 and Scottish Power rose seven pence to 347-1/2.
Southern Electric and Yorkshire Electricity also notched up gains.

"We've seen a lot of interest in the sector all week," one market-maker said. "It's immune from the sterling worries which have been plaguing some sectors and there have been a few recommendations to keep interest up."
On Wednesday, analysts at SBC Warburg highlighted United Utilities as one of their key tips for 1997.
They said it was the most likely share in the electricity and water sectors to outperform ths year and suggested a 700p target price.
Analysts at ABN Amro Hoare Govett, however, reverted to a more neutral stance on the water sector on Friday after becoming more positive in the last quarter of 1996.

They downgraded Yorkshire Water and Anglian Water to "undervalued" from "buy" and said Severn Trent remained the key buy in the sector, while United Utilities and South West Water were undervalued and remained key sells.
